title: Consolidated Workspace Switcher + Role-Aware Sidebar Flow
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and validate a consolidated workspace switching pattern and a role-aware sidebar routing model that reduces friction for multi-workspace users and surfaces role-relevant destinations (dashboards, rollouts, cost views) with predictable keyboard and screen-reader behavior. This ticket contains prototypes, review notes, and a recommended rollout plan for the Console IA change.
goals: Reduce time-to-target (nav -> dashboard/rollouts/cost view) for users that operate across 3+ workspaces
Make primary console destinations discoverable while preserving quick access to workspace-level controls
Support role-based entry points: engineers see runtime and logs, finance sees cost and billing, platform sees rollouts and routes
Ensure keyboard-first navigation and screen-reader semantics for the new switcher and sidebar
scope: Primary sidebar layout and routing rules
Workspace switcher component and contextual menu
Role-awareness mapping and default landing rules
Prototype flows for Dashboard, Rollouts, and Cost pages
Accessibility tests and keyboard nav prototypes
acceptance_criteria: Clickable workspace switcher that shows user workspaces, last-used workspace, and an option to 'Open in new tab'
Sidebar adapts to user role with a stable primary nav order and a collapsible secondary section
Routing rules that preserve deep links when switching workspaces (e.g. /workspace/:id/rollouts/:rolloutId remains valid)
Figma prototype validated by at least two PMs, two engineers, and accessibility reviewer
Performance: sidebar expand/collapse under 50ms on typical dev workstation
Rollout plan documented with canary gating and telemetry events to measure navigation success metrics
design_decisions: Use a single persistent left rail anchored to the viewport to reduce context shift
Expose workspace switcher as a compact token with long-press/keyboard open for fast switching
Role mapping is client-driven with server-provided role tags to avoid duplicate logic in console codepaths
Keep breadcrumbs and URL canonicalization to ensure deep links and copies are stable across workspaces
tradeoffs: Favoring single rail reduces initial discoverability of some workspace-specific tools — mitigated via contextual secondary section
Client-driven role mapping speeds iteration but requires a small contract change from backend to include role tags
Persisting rail state across pages adds complexity to router but improves perceived stability for users
